Priêre en entrant dans le Temple, a paraliturgical Mah Tovu by Rabbi Arnaud Aron & Jonas Ennery (1848)

tei:div.tei:head: Priêre en entrant dans le Temple, a paraliturgical Mah Tovu by Rabbi Arnaud Aron & Jonas Ennery (1848)

tei:l.tei:note: Prayer as you enter the Temple.

tei:lg.tei:l: I rejoice when they say to me,
‘Let’s go to the House of YHVH.’ (Psalms 122:1)

“How beautiful are your dwellings, YHVH! my soul is lifted up to you, and my heart rejoices when I come near your sanctuary. Blessed are they that sojourn in your house, and sing your praises continually. Blessed is the man who seeks his salvation only in you, the eternal shield of Yisrael.”
It is in pronouncing these words of Scripture that I dare, Hashem, to come to this holy place and humbly address my prayer to you, my God, my protector and saviour.

El Shadai, if the whole universe is your Temple; if the world you have created is the altar where your glory shines, it is in the heart of man that you have preferably raised the sanctuary where you want to be adored with holy and pure prayer.
But it is above all to the descendants of the patriarchs, to the servants of the One God to sound your praises, to proclaim your greatness.

Hashem, grant me a pure heart and penetrate it with your spirit, so that no worldly thought may pursue me to that sacred place. It is in your temple that I must remember that a contrite soul is the best of offerings, and repentance the most effective of prayers. Penetrate me, penetrate all my brothers here gathered, with feelings of your greatness and our humility, so that our heads bow before your majesty, and that from the depths of our hearts, holy and collected, our prayer, like divine incense, rises towards your heavenly throne. Amen.
